recent_events.title: Ayil Bank officially renamed to ABank
recent_events.description: On March 12, 2026, the National Bank of Kyrgyzstan replaced the bank's licenses, formally completing the re-registration. The institution now operates under the brand ABank OJSC, reflecting a modernisation of brand identity while preserving all legal obligations, accounts, and agreements. The decision was originally taken at the extraordinary shareholders' meeting on February 2, 2026.
recent_events.impact: Brand refresh after nearly 20 years as Ayil Bank; signals transition from a purely agricultural lender to a universal digital bank; no impact on customers or contracts

recent_events.title: ABank expands preferential agricultural lending program
recent_events.description: ABank launched a new preferential lending program providing subsidised loans to farmers for crop and livestock production and the adoption of modern agricultural technologies, reinforcing its traditional mandate as the country's leading agricultural bank.
recent_events.impact: Strengthens the bank's core rural finance mission and supports national food security goals

recent_events.title: ABank reports record 2025 financial results — net profit of 8.3 billion KGS
recent_events.description: At the annual general shareholders' meeting on March 31, 2026, ABank announced 2025 results: net profit of 8.3 billion soms, total assets of 200.4 billion soms, deposit portfolio of 156 billion soms. The bank confirmed its position as one of the largest banks in Kyrgyzstan by assets.
recent_events.impact: Record profitability reflects successful strategy of product diversification, digitalisation, and innovation; dividends flow to the state budget as the bank is 100% state-owned

recent_events.title: Net profit reaches 7.8 billion KGS for the first 11 months of 2025
recent_events.description: Chairman Tilek Alimdzhanov announced at a press conference at Kabar news agency that for the first 11 months of 2025: net profit reached 7.8 billion soms, assets — 199.5 billion soms, loan portfolio — 85.5 billion soms, deposit portfolio — 152.5 billion soms, equity capital — 29.4 billion soms.
recent_events.impact: Confirms sustained double-digit growth and the bank's leadership in the Kyrgyz banking sector

recent_events.title: Change in the Management Board — Marlis Usenov relieved
recent_events.description: At the Board of Directors meeting on February 12, 2026, Marlis Usenov was removed from his position as Managing Director and member of the Management Board. No replacement was immediately named.
recent_events.impact: Adjustment in senior management composition during the rebranding transition period

recent_events.title: Tilek Alimdzhanov appointed Chairman of the Management Board
recent_events.description: Following the resignation of Maksat Erzhanov after only three months in the role, the Board of Directors appointed Tilek Alimdzhanov as Chairman of the Management Board of OJSC Aiyl Bank, effective late November 2022.
recent_events.impact: Brought experienced banking executive to lead the bank through a period of modernisation and digital transformation

core_business: Universal commercial bank with a specialised mission in agricultural and rural finance. Core operations include: (1) agricultural lending — subsidised state-programme loans to farmers, agribusinesses, and rural producers; (2) leasing of agricultural machinery and equipment (market leader in Kyrgyzstan); (3) retail banking — deposits, consumer loans, money transfers, mobile and online banking; (4) corporate banking — trade finance, investment banking, asset management; (5) Islamic banking products overseen by an in-house Sharia Council. The bank operates the largest rural branch network in the country (37 branches, 60 savings banks, 32 field cash desks, 25 regional and 30 rural credit units). As the sole state-owned universal bank and the country's largest bank by assets (200.4 billion KGS at end-2025), it is the primary vehicle for state-subsidised lending programmes and international donor-funded rural finance projects.
apec_stance: While ABank is not a direct APEC member or participant, it occupies a strategically central role in Central Asian rural and agricultural finance — a priority area for APEC-affiliated development partners active in the Kyrgyz Republic. The bank serves as the on-lending channel for rural finance projects funded by the Asian Development Bank (ADB), World Bank, EBRD, Eurasian Development Bank, and the State Development Bank of China. Through these partnerships, ABank implements donor-funded programmes targeting agricultural modernisation, food security, financial inclusion, and SME development — themes that align with APEC's regional cooperation agenda. In 2026, the bank expanded preferential lending for crop and livestock production and adoption of modern agricultural technologies, reinforcing its function as the key financial bridge between international development assistance and rural Kyrgyz communities.
profile: ABank (formerly Ayil Bank / Айыл Банк) is the largest state-owned commercial bank in Kyrgyzstan and the country's leading institution for agricultural and rural finance. Founded in 1996 with World Bank support as the Kyrgyz Agricultural Finance Corporation (KAFC / КСФК), the institution was reorganised into a universal bank on 27 December 2006 by National Bank Decree No. 43/1. In March 2026, the bank was officially renamed ABank OJSC to mark its evolution from a specialised agricultural lender into a modern universal bank. The Government of the Kyrgyz Republic (Cabinet of Ministers) is the sole shareholder, holding 100% of equity. Headquartered in Bishkek, the bank operates the most extensive branch network in the country with over 160 outlets serving rural communities. Under Chairman of the Management Board Tilek Alimdzhanov (appointed November 2022), the bank reported record 2025 results — net profit of 8.3 billion KGS and total assets of 200.4 billion KGS — confirming its position as the largest bank in Kyrgyzstan by assets. The bank maintains strategic partnerships with major international financial institutions (ADB, World Bank, EBRD, EDB, State Development Bank of China, Russian-Kyrgyz Development Fund, UNDP, Raiffeisen Fund) and is the primary vehicle for state-subsidised lending programmes and donor-funded rural development projects.
